newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-ASM Litho first half net profits up strongly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ASM Litho first half net profits up strongly.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography NV reported first-half earnings above market forecasts on Wednesday and said it saw "clear" growth in its markets.
ASML, in which Philips Electronics holds a 24 percent stake, said first-half net profit rose to 147 million guilders ($71.7 million) from 101 million in the same period of 1996.
After stripping out 31 million guilders of extraordinary income from the sale of a stake in a supplier, earnings were still above analysts' forecasts of 95 to 105 million guilders.

ASM Litho develops and sells photolithography projection systems that are vital to the production of semiconductors, the "chips" which lie at the heart of electronic devices ranging from toasters to mobile phones and computers.
"We're seeing demand picking up. We expect 1997 to show clear growth compared to 1996," ASML chief executive Willem Maris told journalists at a results presentation.
Maris said the semiconductor equipment market always lagged behind the actual semiconductor market, which declined in March 1996 and started to recover at the beginning of this year.

"The equipment market started to decline in the second half of 1996. The first half of this year was pretty lean but we came through it very well because we were able to deliver new technology," Maris said.
In the first half of 1997 the company shipped 95 machines, compared with 98 in the first half of 1996, but it said the decrease was more than offset by a higher average selling price.
The higher price reflected increased shipments of advanced 0.25 micron deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems, it added.

Maris said the shipping of more DUV systems, which currently have slightly lower margins than the older "I-Line" technology, dented gross margins which dipped to 40 percent in the first half from 41.8 percent in the same period a year earlier.
Maris said the company had a strategic target for gross margins of 45 percent but declined to say when that might be reached.

"We think that 45 percent when you look to the equipment industry is a very reasonable gross margin. It is higher, by the way, than what (market leader) Nikon is doing," Maris told Reuters immediately after the news conference.
Maris said ASML was continuing to gain market share against its main rivals, advancing towards its strategic aim of overhauling number two equipment maker Canon.

"I don't know exactly how much we're gaining on Canon. We are gaining on them. The reason is that we have new customers coming in and we're not losing any. We've taken customers in the past from Canon and Nikon," he said.
ASM Litho said it won orders for 136 wafer steppers during the first half of 1997, versus 101 in the first half of 1996.
This led to an order backlog of 135 units, worth 1.27 billion guilders, at the end of June, up from 94 units, worth 688 million guilders, at the end of December.
"After a slow start in 1997, business conditions have solidified and the company is building backlog," Maris said.
The Amsterdam bourse welcomed the news sending ASML shares spurting 23.2 guilders higher to 185.00 guilders before they settled back to 178.50.
"The figures were very pleasing," said one London-based analyst. "I think the stock price can go to between 200 and 225 guilders," he added.
"We had a pretty good feeling about what was going on," said another analyst who declined to be named.

"We talked to the company a couple of weeks ago and it was clear that the second quarter showed a very strong improvement compared to the first two months and that was a reason for us to increase our estimates. We will be looking at upgrading them slightly for the year."
ASML in January reported net income for 1996 of 218 million guilders.
